<content>
1: # Original web sources: Firecrawl and Tavily
2: 
3: ## Integration contract
4: 
5: The factories return the final `ProviderAdapter` contract from
6: `packages/blocks/src/research/provider.ts`:
7: 
8: - `packages/blocks/src/research/providers/firecrawl.ts`: `createFirecrawlAdapter(): ProviderAdapter`
9: - `packages/blocks/src/research/providers/tavily.ts`: `createTavilyAdapter(): ProviderAdapter`
10: 
11: Both use only `ctx.credentials` and `ctx.http.json`. They do not read environment variables, use
12: global `fetch`, log secrets, or require a provider SDK. The caller owns provider selection,
13: configuration/approval gating, query construction, and persistence. The injected HTTP client owns
14: transport deadlines, retries, request accounting, and the shared budget. The adapters also stop
15: before sending a request when `ctx.http.requests` reaches `maxRequests`.
16: 
17: Firecrawl serves `owner_forums`, `editorial_reviews`, `competitor_models`, `market_studies`,
18: `regional_context`, `technology`, `bmw_sales`, and `bmw_strategy` through the same implementation.
19: It uses the supplied `request.queries`; it does not add sentiment-leading searches or substitute
20: agent-specific evidence categories. Scope domains, publication bounds, languages, and explicit URLs
21: are used where supported. Brand, vehicle, market, generation, and research questions belong to the
22: caller’s neutral query construction, not inferred attributes of collected pages. `EU` is not
23: silently translated to a particular country.
24: 
25: ## Official documentation checked
26: 
27: Checked **2026-10-10**, using public documentation only. No requests were made with application
28: credentials, and no live connection or collection was run.
29: 
30: - Firecrawl v2 Search: <https://docs.firecrawl.dev/api-reference/endpoint/search>
31: - Firecrawl two-step search and cost guidance: <https://docs.firecrawl.dev/features/search>
32: - Firecrawl v2 Scrape: <https://docs.firecrawl.dev/api-reference/endpoint/scrape>
33: - Firecrawl Scrape OpenAPI, including the PDF parser fields:
34:   <https://docs.firecrawl.dev/api-reference/endpoint/scrape.md>
35: - Tavily Search: <https://docs.tavily.com/documentation/api-reference/endpoint/search>
36: - Tavily Extract:
37:   <https://docs.tavily.com/documentation/api-reference/endpoint/extract.md>
38: 
39: The Firecrawl reference is authoritative for the v2 `data.web` envelope. Some examples on its
40: feature page still show an older flat `data` array; this adapter deliberately rejects that shape.
41: No Firecrawl `research` category is requested, so its announced November 2026 response change does
42: not affect this adapter.
43: 
44: ## Firecrawl collection
45: 
46: 1. Scrape explicit `scope.urls` first, then search each supplied query with
47:    `POST https://api.firecrawl.dev/v2/search`. Search requests specify `sources: ["web"]`,
48:    `highlights: false`, `domainTools: false`, and no `scrapeOptions` or generated formats.
49: 2. Read `data.web`, validate each source URL, and deduplicate URLs before a paid scrape. Limit each
50:    search to the remaining result budget, capped at the API maximum of 100. Ignore overlong provider
51:    hit arrays beyond the requested limit and report the truncation.
52: 3. Read each eligible original through `POST https://api.firecrawl.dev/v2/scrape`, with
53:    `formats: ["markdown", "rawHtml"]`, `onlyMainContent: false`, `onlyCleanContent: false`, and
54:    `skipTlsVerification: false`. Keeping the entire page avoids dropping forum context or tables.
55:    The raw HTML, actual page metadata, and search discovery metadata remain available in the item.
56:    `maxAge` uses `cacheMaxAgeMs` (default 0); provider cache metadata is preserved when supplied.
57: 4. Always send `parsers: [{ type: "pdf", maxPages: maxDocumentPages, pages: true }]`, including for
58:    URLs without a `.pdf` suffix. The live v2 API accepts a parser object with `maxPages` from 1 to
59:    10,000, not a top-level `pdfOptions`. ReqFlow’s contract limits the requested value to 500.
60:    Returned page markdown is retained in metadata. Responses exceeding the cap are rejected;
61:    `totalPages > numPages` makes the retained document explicitly partial.
62: 
63: One record contains the returned document markdown unchanged, including multilingual passages and
64: table markdown. No generated summary, structured AI extraction, or snippet is used as record text.
65: Missing original markdown is an error, even when search snippets or raw HTML exist.
66: 
67: ## Tavily is an explicit alternative
68: 
69: `POST https://api.tavily.com/search` uses `search_depth: "basic"`, `topic: "general"`,
70: `auto_parameters: false`, `include_answer: false`, and `include_raw_content: "markdown"`.
71: Each search requests at most 20 results. Only nonempty `results[].raw_content` becomes evidence.
72: The `content` field is retained as search metadata, never substituted for a missing original.
73: Returned generated answers are ignored. Publication dates are requested but explicitly identified
74: as Tavily estimates that may describe an update rather than the original publication.
75: 
76: Explicit URLs use Tavily’s own `/extract`, one URL per request, with `extract_depth: "basic"` and
77: `format: "markdown"`. There is no `query` argument, so extraction does not request reranked chunks
78: instead of the full original. Both `results` and `failed_results` are checked, including HTTP-200
79: failures. A missing search original does **not** trigger an extraction purchase or Firecrawl call.
80: 
81: Tavily does not document a numeric PDF page cap. Known `.pdf` URLs and returned PDF content types
82: are excluded with a limitation; select Firecrawl explicitly for bounded PDF collection. PDFs behind
83: extensionless URLs cannot reliably be identified or page-bounded through Tavily’s documented
84: response. No automatic switch to Firecrawl is implemented, even if both credentials are present.
85: 
86: ## Provenance, scope, and access limits
87: 
88: - Preserve the requested source URL, original text, supplied title/publisher/language/date, and
89:   actual metadata. A safe final redirect URL remains separately available as `metadata.finalUrl`.
90:   An absent title falls back to the source URL, not a fabricated document title.
91: - Records conservatively use `recordType: "passage"` and `sourceKind: "other_web"`. Agent names,
92:   search rank, requested vehicle, or domain names are not evidence types. An official product
93:   description must be explicit in the original source before downstream classification; choosing
94:   `competitor_models` does not make a page a product description. Search categories, when supplied
95:   by the provider, are retained only as discovery metadata.
96: - No market, vehicle, publication date, sentiment, score interpretation, or reliability is invented.
97:   Missing publication is `datePrecision: "unknown"`. Unknown or coarse dates within a requested
98:   date window are retained with a limitation, not assigned retrieval time. Known dates outside the
99:   window are excluded. Provider search date filtering alone does not prove source publication.
100: - Enforce allowed and blocked hostnames on discovered URLs, explicit URLs, and supplied
101:   `metadata.url`/`metadata.sourceURL`. Domain matching respects label boundaries and includes
102:   subdomains. Block rules take precedence. Firecrawl makes its include/exclude request fields
103:   mutually exclusive; the adapter sends include rules when both are configured and enforces both
104:   locally. Tavily supports both fields. Filters must be hostnames, not paths, wildcards, or URLs.
105: - Only public HTTP(S) hostname URLs without credentials or custom ports are accepted. Local names,
106:   reserved local suffixes, and all IP literals are rejected, including IPv6 and URL-normalized
107:   integer/hex IP forms. This is intentionally stricter than allowing public IP literals.
108: - Top-level API success is distinct from target access. Target `metadata.statusCode` must be 2xx
109:   when provided. Target errors, non-2xx bodies, recognizable access-denied/anti-bot documents, and
110:   empty originals are not evidence. Missing target status or final redirect URL makes a retained
111:   original partial, not an unqualified success. Requested but absent raw HTML is also a Firecrawl
112:   limitation for non-PDF pages.
113: - Tavily’s documented search/extract results do not promise target status or final redirect URL.
114:   Ordinary Tavily collection therefore reports those access limitations and is normally partial,
115:   even when useful original text is retained. Any such metadata actually returned is validated.
116: - URL checks cannot observe vendor-side DNS resolution or prevent DNS rebinding/hidden redirects
117:   before the vendor fetches a target. They reject detected unsafe targets before persistence. They
118:   are not a replacement for vendor network isolation. Challenge detection is conservative, not a
119:   guarantee that every soft-blocked page can be identified.
120: - Paywalls, logins, robots restrictions, anti-bot controls, missing forum pagination, hidden comments,
121:   OCR errors, and provider-cleaned content can limit access or completeness. Neither adapter claims
122:   to collect an entire discussion, crawl every linked page, authenticate to a source, or bypass
123:   access controls. A successful page read does not prove its claims or settle conflicting evidence.
124: 
125: Collections run sequentially, within result and request bounds. They pass `ctx.signal` on every
126: request and retain previously read originals after a later request failure, exhausted budget, or
127: cancellation. Affected runs are partial instead of losing all successful hits. Valid empty searches
128: are `empty`; malformed API envelopes are `error`; missing keys cause no requests.
129: 
130: ## Connection tests and possible cost
131: 
132: Each `test(ctx)` sends only one deterministic query, `site:example.com Example Domain`, with one
133: result, no scrape, and no generated answer. Empty but valid search results still prove API access.
134: The test validates the protocol and reports missing/invalid credentials, permission failures, rate
135: limits, or unreachable APIs without echoing provider error bodies or keys.
136: 
137: These are **not free credential checks**. Firecrawl documents 2 credits per 1–10 search results,
138: rounded up; a one-result probe can cost 2 credits. Its regular HTML scrape costs 1 credit per page,
139: and PDF parsing costs 1 credit per parsed PDF page. Tavily documents 1 credit for a basic search and
140: 1 credit per 5 successful basic URL extractions. Account rounding, retries, plan rules, and future
141: pricing changes can affect billing. Request/result/page limits are not an exact financial cap;
142: the injected HTTP budget and provider account limits must remain in force.
143: 
144: ## Offline proof
145: 
146: ```sh
147: npx vitest run packages/blocks/src/research/providers/firecrawl.test.ts packages/blocks/src/research/providers/tavily.test.ts
148: ```
149: 
150: Tests inject deterministic HTTP responses. They cover multilingual originals and tables, unknown
151: publication, missing/invalid keys, target 403 and other failures, empty originals, snippets and
152: generated answers, malformed protocols, partial results, URL/domain/redirect policy, request and
153: result limits, PDF caps, explicit URLs, cancellation, and the small connection-test request shapes.
154: No test requires an API key or network access.
</content>

1: # Official social provider adapters
2: 
3: ## Scope and implementation plan
4: 
5: This slice owns only `youtube.ts`, `x.ts`, `reddit.ts`, their colocated tests in
6: `packages/blocks/src/research/providers/`, and this document. Shared contracts,
7: manifests, workstream status, user files, branches, and commits remain untouched.
8: 
9: 1. Independently check official API documentation and the shared contracts.
10: 2. Write offline contract and pagination tests using synthetic credentials.
11: 3. Implement the three factories through the injected `ProviderContext` HTTP client.
12: 4. Run focused tests, repository typecheck and tests; document limits and handoff.
13: 
14: No live credential tests or confidential data access are authorized for this slice.
15: 
16: ## Exports and integration
17: 
18: - `packages/blocks/src/research/providers/youtube.ts`: `createYouTubeAdapter(): ProviderAdapter`
19: - `packages/blocks/src/research/providers/x.ts`: `createXAdapter(): ProviderAdapter`
20: - `packages/blocks/src/research/providers/reddit.ts`: `createRedditAdapter(): ProviderAdapter`
21: 
22: Factories take no keys and do not read environment variables. The main process
23: injects credentials, configuration, limits, clock, cancellation signal, and HTTP
24: client. All requests use `ctx.http.json` with explicit method, headers and signal.
25: Reddit's OAuth request additionally supplies a URL-encoded **string** body; the
26: shared HTTP client must transmit string bodies unchanged, not JSON-encode them.
27: The registry/main-process wiring is outside this slice's ownership.
28: 
29: Collection checks `config.enabled`. Connection tests intentionally work without
30: enabling collection, but Reddit's approval gate still applies. Boundary input and
31: provider response shapes are validated with Zod. Each output record is parsed
32: with the shared `CollectedItem` schema.
33: 
34: Only fixed HTTPS provider hosts receive requests. Reddit thread paths contain
35: validated ID36 identifiers, not provider-supplied permalinks. Queries are supplied
36: unchanged; the adapters do not add positive/negative, sentiment or ownership
37: filters. No scraping fallback, model call, source credibility score, sentiment,
38: inferred market, or inferred vehicle/ownership classification is added.
39: 
40: ## YouTube Data API v3
41: 
42: Credential: `youtube_api_key`, transmitted in `X-Goog-Api-Key`, not in the URL.
43: 
44: 1. `GET /youtube/v3/search`: `part=snippet`, `type=video`, supplied `q`, bounded
45:    `maxResults`, optional video publication dates, and `pageToken`.
46: 2. `GET /youtube/v3/videos`: batch hydration with `part=snippet` and video IDs.
47:    The full author description is a separate `metadata` record. The video title,
48:    channel ID/name, publication time, default text language and default audio
49:    language remain metadata. Audio language is not treated as text language.
50: 3. `GET /youtube/v3/commentThreads`: `part=snippet,replies`, `textFormat=plainText`,
51:    `videoId`, and paginated thread results. Top-level audience comments and
52:    embedded replies become independent `feedback` records.
53: 4. If embedded distinct replies are fewer than `totalReplyCount`,
54:    `GET /youtube/v3/comments` with `parentId` follows **every** `nextPageToken`
55:    until completion or an injected limit/failure. Embedded and fetched comments
56:    are deduplicated by original comment ID. Embedded partial replies are never
57:    treated as the complete thread.
58: 
59: Source/video, record/comment, parent and thread IDs remain provider IDs.
60: Publication timestamps and available author metadata remain intact. Reply
61: context contains the top-level comment; top-level context identifies the video
62: description. Comment language is unknown: video language and query language do
63: not establish audience language. Publication search dates constrain videos, not
64: the dates of all comments on those videos; comment timestamps remain explicit.
65: 
66: `textOriginal` is used when returned. Official documentation says it is only
67: available to the comment's author. Most public responses instead contain
68: `textDisplay`: this is requested as plain text and retained exactly as returned,
69: with a per-record warning that it may differ from the author's original text.
70: No HTML stripping, translation or text reconstruction is performed.
71: 
72: **Transcripts are not available without supported authorized captions access.**
73: This adapter has only an API-key contract, not an authorized captions credential.
74: It does not call captions endpoints, reconstruct arbitrary transcripts, or
75: represent descriptions/comments as transcripts. Deleted/private videos, disabled
76: comments, moderated/deleted replies and search coverage can prevent complete
77: collection. Hydration gaps and short reply counts are reported as partial.
78: 
79: Connection test: one `videos.list(part=id, chart=mostPopular, maxResults=1)` request.
80: It consumes quota and does not prove permissions for every video's comments or
81: for subsequent searches.
82: 
83: ## X API v2
84: 
85: Credential: `x_bearer_token`, transmitted as `Authorization: Bearer …`.
86: 
87: `config.xSearchMode` selects exactly one endpoint:
88: 
89: - `recent`: `GET https://api.x.com/2/tweets/search/recent`, last seven days only.
90: - `full_archive`: `GET https://api.x.com/2/tweets/search/all`, account access required.
91: 
92: The adapter requests `created_at`, `conversation_id`, `in_reply_to_user_id`,
93: `referenced_tweets`, `author_id`, `lang`, original `text` and `note_tweet`, plus
94: author/referenced-post expansions. Author identifiers and returned names,
95: handles and free-form location remain metadata. Location does not establish a
96: market. Reply parent IDs, conversation IDs, reference types, original timestamps
97: and provider language tags remain intact. Returned expanded parent text is
98: context; missing parent text is not fabricated or independently scraped.
99: 
100: `note_tweet.text` takes precedence for long posts. The short `text` field is also
101: retained in metadata. Some generated current references use `note_post`,
102: `referenced_posts` and `includes.posts`; returned aliases are accepted. Requests
103: use the `tweet.fields`/`referenced_tweets.id` names verified in the official recent
104: and archive quickstarts and data dictionary. The generated recent endpoint
105: reference currently differs in its Post naming; no speculative retry with a
106: different request contract is performed.
107: 
108: Pagination follows `meta.next_token`, retains supplied query/date parameters,
109: deduplicates post IDs, and stops at injected limits. The API minimum page size
110: is ten posts even when `limits.maxResults` is smaller; only the allowed number of
111: records is emitted. No tariff or currency cost is hardcoded. Bounded requests
112: **can bill**; request limits are not a guarantee of a particular monetary cost.
113: 
114: An explicit publication start older than the recent window, an end entirely
115: outside that window, or a future start returns `blocked` before HTTP. The
116: adapter does not silently move a historical start into the recent window.
117: Inclusive `publishedTo` days become exclusive next-day `end_time` values. An end
118: on the current/future day stops ten seconds before the injected clock and is
119: explicitly disclosed. Recent mode without explicit dates still reports its
120: seven-day limitation. Archive 403 returns `blocked`; it never falls back to
121: recent search. A later 403 preserves earlier records and returns `partial`.
122: 
123: Connection test: one minimum-size search (`query=BMW`, `max_results=10`) on the
124: **configured endpoint**. This may bill and does not test a different access mode.
125: 
126: ## Reddit Data API
127: 
128: Collection and connection tests require `config.approval === "granted"` and all
129: three injected credentials: `reddit_client_id`, `reddit_client_secret` and
130: `reddit_refresh_token`. Missing refresh tokens never yield success. Approval
131: must represent permission for this specific use, not merely OAuth consent or an
132: app registration. Current Reddit policy distinguishes commercial data-use
133: permission and the Reddit For Researchers program; a local flag cannot acquire
134: permission or prove eligibility. Do not enable this adapter without the
135: applicable permission. No provider terms are accepted automatically.
136: 
137: Authentication uses documented OAuth refresh only:
138: 
139: - `POST https://www.reddit.com/api/v1/access_token`
140: - HTTP Basic client ID/secret; configured `redditUserAgent` on every request.
141: - `Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded`
142: - Body: `grant_type=refresh_token&refresh_token=…`
143: - Returned Bearer token must have `read` (or `*`) scope.
144: 
145: There are no user passwords, client-credentials substitution, unauthenticated
146: successes, or environment-derived secrets. Access tokens are held only within
147: the current call, not persisted or logged.
148: 
149: Search uses `GET https://oauth.reddit.com/search.json`, `q`, `type=link`, `sort=new`,
150: `t=all`, bounded `limit`, and listing `after`/`count` pagination. `raw_json=1`
151: avoids Reddit's legacy HTML entity substitutions. Original submission body (or
152: title when the body is empty), author, subreddit, IDs, permalink and UTC
153: timestamp are preserved. Arbitrary publication ranges are filtered locally;
154: the API's search coverage and date-filter limitations remain explicit.
155: 
156: Each selected thread uses `GET /comments/{ID36}.json`, `sort=new`, bounded `limit`
157: and `showmore=true`. Returned nested comments are walked as a tree. Original
158: comment bodies, fullname IDs, parent IDs, link/thread IDs, timestamps and
159: available parent/thread context are retained. Removed/deleted placeholders are
160: not treated as evidence. Reddit does not supply reliable per-comment language
161: or market in this API; both remain unknown.
162: 
163: **MoreComments expansion is not implemented.** Every encountered stub, including
164: nested stubs, marks the result `partial` and identifies the thread in limitations.
165: The supported future extension is serialized, bounded `/api/morechildren` calls
166: with at most 100 ID36 children per request. Comment-tree endpoints do not document
167: listing-style `after` pagination; unexpected comment/reply cursors also mark the
168: result partial rather than silently discarding the continuation. Submission
169: search pages do use `after` pagination. No claim of complete Reddit conversation
170: coverage is made.
171: 
172: Connection test: OAuth refresh plus one OAuth search with `limit=1`. It requires
173: `read`, not the unrelated `identity` scope used by `/api/v1/me`. Account-specific
174: fees and access restrictions may still apply.
175: 
176: ## Failure, cancellation and bounds
177: 
178: `ctx.http` owns retries, provider budget enforcement, rate-limit handling and
179: timeouts. Adapters add no retries, sleeps, direct fetches or parallel unbounded
180: requests. They check cancellation and the shared request counter before every
181: request; `maxResults` bounds all emitted records, including video metadata.
182: Repeated pagination cursors stop collection instead of looping.
183: 
184: If a later page/request fails, prior records remain in `items` with `partial`.
185: Cancellation always returns `cancelled`, retaining prior records. Initial rejected
186: credentials return `missing_credentials`; initial permission denial returns
187: `blocked`; other initial failures return `error`. A reached collection bound is
188: explicitly partial, not a claim of complete collection. Malformed provider JSON
189: does not become synthetic evidence or an empty success.
190: 
191: Connection reports use core states: missing configuration `not_configured`, 401
192: `invalid_credentials`, 403 `permission_required`, 429 `rate_limited`, and transport
193: or malformed-response failures `unreachable`. Cancelled/limit-stopped tests use
194: `unreachable` with the precise stop code in a safe message, since core has no
195: cancelled connection state. Known `ProviderError` codes are preserved.
196: 
197: Only fixed messages and stop codes enter logs/reports. Raw exception messages,
198: provider error bodies, credentials and request headers are never logged.
199:

1: # Publication, statistics and local document collection
2: 
3: These adapters return provider-owned original records through the final `ProviderAdapter` contract.
4: They do not classify opinions with AI, infer preferences from statistics, create forecasts, approve
5: requirements, or execute instructions contained in collected documents. All filesystem and subprocess
6: operations belong in the Electron main process.
7: 
8: ## Exported factories and integration
9: 
10: ```ts
11: // packages/blocks/src/research/providers/openalex.ts
12: createOpenAlexAdapter(): ProviderAdapter
13: // packages/blocks/src/research/providers/eurostat.ts
14: createEurostatAdapter(): ProviderAdapter
15: // packages/blocks/src/research/providers/documents.ts
16: createLocalDocumentsAdapter(): ProviderAdapter
17: 
18: // packages/blocks/src/research/documents/local.ts
19: interface LocalDocumentReaderOptions {
20:   resolveFile: (id: string) => Promise<{ path: string; name: string }>;
21:   doclingCommand?: string;
22:   xlsxWorkerPath?: string;
23: }
24: createLocalDocumentReader(
25:   options: LocalDocumentReaderOptions,
26: ): NonNullable<ProviderContext["documents"]>
27: ```
28: 
29: The parent supplies `resolveFile` from its trusted imported-file store. Renderer inputs are imported
30: `file_…` IDs only; the renderer never supplies a path or executable. The resolver must return an
31: absolute path to a regular, non-symlink file. An executable setting is main-process configuration,
32: not a document or renderer instruction. Use an absolute executable path when it is outside `PATH`.
33: 
34: ```ts
35: const reader = createLocalDocumentReader({
36:   resolveFile: (id) => importedFiles.resolve(id),
37:   xlsxWorkerPath: join(__dirname, "research-xlsx-worker.js"),
38: });
39: // Supply this same reader through ProviderContext.documents for both BMW agents.
40: const documents = reader;
41: ```
42: 
43: Cache document reads **in the parent run**, keyed by imported file ID and page limit. Share an
44: in-flight promise between `bmw_sales` and `bmw_strategy` when both select the same imported ID.
45: Scope that cache to a run with a shared run abort signal, remove failed promises, and do not reuse
46: cancelled promises across runs. The reader deliberately does not maintain a persistent content cache.
47: This preserves original source/record IDs and lets the parent deduplicate records while retaining
48: both collecting-agent associations. Adapters neither infer an import's BMW dataset kind from its
49: filename nor independently count repeated sheet associations as opinions.
50: 
51: Source identity uses `reqflow-file:///<fileId>`, not `file://` URLs containing private user paths.
52: `sourceTitle` is the imported ID. `metadata.originalArtifact = { fileId }` points back to the parent
53: file store; temporary conversion artifacts are not source identities. Table sheet names, row numbers,
54: Docling JSON pointers, page numbers and bounding boxes remain available for evidence lookup.
55: 
56: ## OpenAlex
57: 
58: Verified against official documentation on 2026-10-10:
59: 
60: - [Search works](https://docs.openalex.org/api-entities/works/search-works).
61: - [Cursor pagination](https://docs.openalex.org/how-to-use-the-api/get-lists-of-entities/paging).
62: - [Work attributes](https://docs.openalex.org/api-entities/works/work-object).
63: - [Authentication](https://docs.openalex.org/how-to-use-the-api/rate-limits-and-authentication).
64: 
65: Collection uses `GET https://api.openalex.org/works`, `search`, publication-date/language `filter`,
66: `cursor=*`, and response `meta.next_cursor`. Page size is at most the currently supported 100.
67: Queries come from the supplied query plan, scope questions, scope keywords, or vehicle/market scope;
68: no unrelated default research topic is substituted. Publication-date and supported two-letter
69: language filters come from scope. Geographic applicability is **not** inferred from author affiliation,
70: query wording, or a requested EU market. Allowed-domain rules cannot constrain OpenAlex's scholarly
71: corpus through these filters; this adapter collects OpenAlex metadata, not arbitrary linked sites.
72: 
73: Optional `openalex_api_key` travels only in the officially supported `Authorization: Bearer …`
74: header, never in a URL, output record, or adapter log. The injected HTTP transport must also redact
75: authorization headers. HTTP failures are converted to fixed, credential-safe messages. Pagination
76: deduplicates work IDs and reports result/request limits, repeated cursors, cancellation and partial
77: page failures explicitly. The connection probe performs one search with `per_page=1&select=id,title`.
78: 
79: `abstract_inverted_index` is reconstructed by position with original tokens and no paraphrasing.
80: Returned text is labeled `ABSTRACT\n…`; `metadata.contentLevel` is `abstract`. Missing or ambiguous
81: indexes yield explicitly labeled metadata-only records. Publication metadata includes title, DOI,
82: authors, bibliographic fields, date/year, language, work type, OA and retraction metadata.
83: 
84: An explicitly OA primary-location PDF URL is preserved only as an **unretrieved original reference**
85: with `accessibility: "provider_metadata"`. Credential-bearing links are not retained. This contract
86: has no remote binary downloader/parser, so this adapter does not download PDFs, scrape landing pages,
87: retrieve OpenAlex metered content, or call local Docling on remote documents. OpenAlex abstracts and
88: OA flags are **not full-text evidence** and do not provide complete commercial market studies.
89: 
90: ## Eurostat
91: 
92: Verified against official documentation on 2026-10-10:
93: 
94: - [Statistics API overview and time filters](https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/web/user-guides/data-browser/api-data-access/api-getting-started/api).
95: - [Statistics API detailed guidelines](https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/web/user-guides/data-browser/api-data-access/api-detailed-guidelines/api-statistics).
96: 
97: Collection requires explicit `scope.eurostatDatasets`, including dataset codes and dimension filters.
98: Without them, the outcome is `blocked` with a selection limitation, not unrelated statistics. Requests
99: use the official Statistics 1.0 JSON-stat 2.0 endpoint with `format=JSON` and an API-supported label
100: language (`EN`, `DE`, `FR`). Geographic filters are passed exactly; `EU` is never expanded to an EU
101: aggregate or country list. `time`/`time_period`, `sinceTimePeriod`, `untilTimePeriod` and
102: `lastTimePeriod` remain explicit dataset selections. Conflicting time modes and simultaneous
103: `geo`/`geoLevel` are rejected. Publication dates are not silently reinterpreted as observation periods.
104: 
105: Each dataset selection produces a raw metrics **table record**, not prose conclusions. Row-major
106: coordinate decoding follows `id` and `size`; both dimension codes and category labels appear in
107: columns. Values remain numeric, zero remains zero, and missing/suppressed observations remain `null`.
108: Observation status strings, including combined flags such as `ep`, are preserved without interpretation.
109: Dimensions, labels, explicit units, notes, annotations, raw sparse/dense values/status and full
110: extensions are retained. `updated` is dataset metadata, not an observation's publication date.
111: 
112: A selection is capped at 20,000 observation cells. Larger or asynchronous extractions produce an
113: explicit limitation requesting narrower filters; no partial table is mislabeled complete. Dataset
114: failures preserve successful preceding selections. The connection probe retrieves a single latest
115: `demo_pjan` observation for `geo=DE&sex=T&age=TOTAL`, not a research run or default dataset suggestion.
116: 
117: ## Local TXT and XLSX
118: 
119: Plain UTF-8 TXT is retained verbatim as one passage. Invalid encoding is rejected rather than
120: silently replacing bytes. Text is never interpreted as executable instructions.
121: 
122: Regular XLSX uses the existing `exceljs` dependency, with deterministic workbook/sheet order.
123: Every sheet is preserved; the first nonempty row is the header, subsequent row positions and values
124: remain exact, including interior blank rows and `null` cells. Empty header cells remain empty strings.
125: This deterministic header rule is stated as a limitation; it is not a semantic header detector.
126: Numbers, booleans, strings, saved formula results, rich text, hyperlink display text and ISO date
127: representations are supported. Formula objects, rich-text/hyperlink artifacts, date formats and cell
128: notes remain in metadata. Formulas, hyperlinks and macros are never executed or followed. Explicit
129: unit columns/header markers and source cell notes populate table units/footnotes. Units are not
130: inferred from a value's magnitude. `maxPages` does not truncate spreadsheet sheets.
131: 
132: The `Feedback_Explorer` layout requires explicit feedback ID, text and VFC columns. Repeated
133: **same ID + same text** rows become one `feedback` record with multiple original VFC associations,
134: row locators and source classifications. Different IDs remain distinct even with identical text;
135: different texts under one ID remain separate and carry a conflict limitation. Classification cells
136: are marked `origin: "source_explicit"`; no AI classification or additional independent opinion is
137: created. Conflicting market/vehicle cells remove single-value attribution but retain original rows.
138: 
139: Files are capped at 64 MiB, each sheet at 100,000 rows and 512 columns. These are fail-explicit safety
140: bounds, not silent truncation. Plain TXT and XLSX need no Python or Docling installation.
141: 
142: ### XLSX memory and execution isolation
143: 
144: The desktop parent must build `packages/blocks/src/research/documents/xlsx-worker.ts` as a separate
145: Node worker entry named **`research-xlsx-worker.js`** and supply its trusted absolute output path as
146: `xlsxWorkerPath`. The worker imports ExcelJS directly; bundle its runtime dependencies or ensure
147: they are resolvable from that output location. Place the entry outside ASAR and keep it independent
148: of renderer code. This slice does not modify Electron/Vite configuration; the parent owns that entry.
149: 
150: With `xlsxWorkerPath`, parsing runs in a real `worker_threads.Worker`, not on the main event loop.
151: The worker receives transferred workbook bytes only, an empty environment (no provider secrets),
152: no inherited `execArgv`, and `workerData: { reqflowXlsxWorker: true }` as its entry marker. The worker
153: has a 128 MiB old-generation heap limit, 16 MiB young-generation limit and 4 MiB stack limit. These
154: V8 limits are **not a total RSS limit**; ZIP buffers/native allocations are separately bounded below.
155: The parent enforces a 30-second parse deadline, promptly terminates CPU-bound workers on cancellation,
156: discards worker stdout/stderr, and converts parser/runtime failures to fixed messages without paths
157: or document text. A configured worker failure never triggers in-process or cloud fallback.
158: 
159: Before starting the worker or ExcelJS, the parent checks ZIP central/local headers. XLSX archives
160: are limited to **16 MiB compressed**, **32 MiB total declared expansion**, and **2,048 entries**.
161: Malformed, encrypted, multi-disk and unsupported compression archives are rejected; Zip64 is explicitly
162: unsupported. Local/central sizes and names must agree, file ranges cannot overlap, and duplicate
163: entry names are rejected. Decompression additionally verifies actual entry length using a bounded
164: zlib output limit before ExcelJS sees the workbook, so under-declared expansion cannot bypass bounds.
165: 
166: Worksheet XML row/cell/dimension addresses are checked before ExcelJS load, and decoded sheet
167: dimensions are checked again after loading. The aggregate budget across **all** sheets is
168: **1,000,000 `rowCount × columnCount` cells**, including sparse gaps; no dense representation is created
169: before that check. Parsed existing-cell metadata is capped at **16 MiB** before worker transfer and
170: revalidated by the parent. The worker returns preserved row/cell data, not an unchecked workbook model.
171: The reader uses existing cells only, never `getCell`/`getRow` to materialize absent cells, and yields
172: periodically while producing bounded null-filled table rows. Feedback records retain only their own
173: association rows/artifacts; they do not clone the entire sheet's row index per opinion.
174: 
175: The optional path preserves in-process compatibility for callers/tests that do not provide a worker.
176: That mode still applies ZIP expansion, pre-load address, output and aggregate cell checks, but does
177: **not** provide the worker's heap isolation or hard termination deadline. Desktop integration must
178: supply `xlsxWorkerPath`; do not use compatibility mode for production untrusted imports. Synthetic
179: CJS worker tests cover real Worker invocation, empty environment, cancellation, deadline and fixed
180: error handling. Native Electron worker bundling/smoke verification remains the parent's integration gate.
181: 
182: ## Optional local Docling subprocess
183: 
184: Verified against official documentation on 2026-10-10:
185: 
186: - [Installation](https://docling-project.github.io/docling/getting_started/installation/).
187: - [CLI reference](https://docling-project.github.io/docling/reference/cli/).
188: - [Model prefetch and offline usage](https://docling-project.github.io/docling/usage/advanced_options/).
189: 
190: PDF/DOCX/PPTX conversion is optional and requires a separately installed **local** Python Docling
191: CLI and prefetched layout/table models. Electron installers do not gain this Python runtime or
192: model assets merely by bundling JavaScript. Packaging must include architecture-compatible Python,
193: Docling/PyTorch dependencies and model artifacts outside the ASAR, or document a local installation.
194: No manifests or installer definitions are changed by this slice.
195: 
196: Example development preparation (an explicit operator action, never an automatic document fallback):
197: 
198: ```sh
199: python -m venv .venv-docling
200: # Activate this environment using your platform's normal command.
201: python -m pip install docling
202: docling-tools models download layout tableformer
203: # Set DOCLING_ARTIFACTS_PATH to an absolute path containing these prefetched artifacts.
204: # On Windows, pass the trusted .venv-docling/Scripts/docling.exe path as doclingCommand.
205: # On macOS/Linux, pass the trusted .venv-docling/bin/docling path as doclingCommand.
206: docling --help
207: ```
208: 
209: Pin and test the chosen Python/Docling/PyTorch versions when packaging. Intel macOS has distinct
210: PyTorch compatibility constraints described in the official installation page. Prefetch happens
211: before sensitive document parsing and may contact model repositories; parsing itself never installs
212: dependencies or downloads assets.
213: 
214: The reader probes help locally (at most two five-second subprocesses), detects the newer `convert`
215: subcommand versus a compatible legacy CLI, and checks required safety/page/export flags. A missing
216: executable, unsupported CLI, or absent absolute `DOCLING_ARTIFACTS_PATH` leaves TXT/XLSX available and
217: reports complex formats unsupported. A help probe does not prove that every required model is
218: installed; missing/incompatible model assets produce an explicit conversion error.
219: 
220: Conversion uses `spawn` with an argument array and `shell: false`, a private temporary directory,
221: a fixed temporary input filename, JSON output, `--page-range 1-N`, a 120-second CLI/process timeout,
222: abort-signal cancellation, and bounded subprocess/output bytes. The subprocess receives only an
223: allowlisted local environment, not provider credentials. Remote services and external plugins are
224: disabled, model-cache offline flags are set, and OCR is disabled in this deliberately narrow slice.
225: Scanned PDFs need a separately approved local OCR integration; no cloud OCR fallback exists. The
226: runtime must be provisioned offline and can additionally be network-sandboxed by packaging policy.
227: 
228: PDF/PPTX page limits are passed to the backend. DOCX does not have stable PDF-style pagination;
229: records state that bounds apply where supported and do not claim complete page coverage. Exported
230: text prefers Docling `orig` over normalized `text`, tables retain cell spans/flags, footnote refs and
231: original text, and records retain JSON pointers/page provenance plus the original imported artifact
232: ID. Temporary files are removed in `finally`, including on cancellation; cleanup failure is explicit.
233: 
234: The current development host has no detected `docling` command. Tests exercise deterministic
235: TXT/XLSX ingestion and a **synthetic local executable** for real subprocess invocation, safety flags,
236: JSON export ingestion and cancellation. They do not claim a real Python/model-backed PDF conversion
237: was run or that Docling is already packaged.
</content>

1: # Apify Instagram and TikTok adapter
2: 
3: ## Interface and approval boundary
4: 
5: `packages/blocks/src/research/providers/apify.ts` exports:
6: 
7: ```ts
8: export function createApifyAdapter(): ProviderAdapter;
9: ```
10: 
11: The factory takes no credentials, actor IDs, actor input overrides, or network client.
12: `collect(request, ctx)` and `test(ctx)` use the shared adapter contract from
13: `packages/blocks/src/research/provider.ts`. Credentials come only from
14: `ctx.credentials.apify_api_token`. All HTTP calls use `ctx.http`; the renderer must
15: not instantiate this adapter.
16: 
17: Collection supports only `request.agentId === "instagram"` or `"tiktok"`. It
18: requires a valid core provider configuration with `enabled: true`,
19: `approval: "granted"`, and the **exact actor being run** in `allowedActors`.
20: Actor selection is hard-coded to the core `APIFY_ACTORS` list:
21: 
22: - `apify/instagram-scraper`
23: - `apify/instagram-comment-scraper`
24: - `clockworks/tiktok-scraper`
25: - `clockworks/tiktok-comments-scraper`
26: 
27: There is no arbitrary actor configuration or fallback actor. Post discovery
28: requires approval for the platform's post actor. The comment actor requires its
29: own allowlist entry; a post actor, valid token, public page, or successful previous
30: run does not imply permission for comments. If the comment actor is not approved,
31: post results are retained with `partial` status and a named limitation. Approving
32: only a comment actor does not enable discovery; that configuration is blocked.
33: Neither configuration nor token authentication establishes legal permission to
34: collect, store, redistribute, or use social content. The operator must check
35: platform terms, actor terms, privacy requirements, and intended usage rights.
36: 
37: ## Official schemas verified
38: 
39: Checked on **2026-10-10** against official actor input/output pages and README
40: examples, independently of ReqFlow's existing research documentation. Only public
41: documentation was fetched. No actor was run and no real token was tested.
42: 
43: Instagram posts:
44: 
45: - [Input schema](https://apify.com/apify/instagram-scraper/input-schema)
46: - [Output schema](https://apify.com/apify/instagram-scraper/output-schema)
47: - [README and output examples](https://apify.com/apify/instagram-scraper)
48: 
49: Instagram comments:
50: 
51: - [Input schema](https://apify.com/apify/instagram-comment-scraper/input-schema)
52: - [Output schema](https://apify.com/apify/instagram-comment-scraper/output-schema)
53: - [README and nested-reply example](https://apify.com/apify/instagram-comment-scraper)
54: 
55: TikTok posts:
56: 
57: - [Input schema](https://apify.com/clockworks/tiktok-scraper/input-schema)
58: - [Output page](https://apify.com/clockworks/tiktok-scraper/output-schema)
59: - [README and output examples](https://apify.com/clockworks/tiktok-scraper)
60: 
61: TikTok comments:
62: 
63: - [Input schema](https://apify.com/clockworks/tiktok-comments-scraper/input-schema)
64: - [Output schema](https://apify.com/clockworks/tiktok-comments-scraper/output-schema)
65: - [README and output example](https://apify.com/clockworks/tiktok-comments-scraper)
66: 
67: The TikTok post output page did not expose usable row definitions in the retrieved
68: content. Its official README provides `id`, `text`, `textLanguage`, `createTime`,
69: `createTimeISO`, `isAd`, `isSponsored`, `webVideoUrl`, and
70: `videoMeta.subtitleLinks`. The adapter validates this documented shape; it does
71: not assume an undocumented generic social-media schema. The Instagram comment
72: README shows `replies` arrays, whereas its current output schema documents
73: `postUrl`, `commentUrl`, `id`, `text`, and `timestamp`. Both forms are supported.
74: The TikTok comment output schema explicitly documents `repliesToId` and
75: `createTime`, in addition to its README's `cid`, `videoWebUrl`, and
76: `createTimeISO`.
77: 
78: The published output schemas make many fields optional or nullable. Collection
79: still needs an original ID and supported source URL to create traceable records.
80: Instagram numeric IDs are accepted only when JavaScript can represent them
81: exactly; unsafe numeric IDs are rejected rather than silently rounded. Large IDs
82: must arrive as strings. Null/missing captions and comment text become empty-text
83: `metadata` records, never fabricated opinions. Error rows without usable evidence
84: are reported rather than converted into records.
85: 
86: Actors run their configured/default build. These public schemas can change;
87: offline tests are compatibility checks against documented examples, not proof
88: that a future build or every account tier returns the same fields.
89: 
90: ## Supported access paths and gaps
91: 
92: When `scope.urls` is nonempty, those URLs take precedence. Unsupported URLs are
93: reported, not replaced with a keyword search. Supported HTTPS URLs have no user
94: credentials or nonstandard port and use the exact bare or `www` platform host.
95: Domain allow/block restrictions apply before actor launch and to returned records.
96: 
97: For Instagram:
98: 
99: - `/p/<shortcode>/` and `/reel/<shortcode>/` post URLs;
100: - public profile URLs, such as `https://www.instagram.com/example/`;
101: - `/explore/tags/<hashtag>/` URLs;
102: - without URLs, **literal `#hashtag` queries only**, using `search`,
103:   `searchType: "hashtag"`, `searchLimit: 1`, `resultsType: "posts"`, and
104:   `resultsLimit`.
105: 
106: Explicit reel URLs use the documented `resultsType: "reels"`; other supported
107: Instagram inputs use `"posts"`. Original `/reel/` context and `/p/` comment
108: permalinks are both retained when they identify the same original shortcode.
109: 
110: The actor documents hashtag/profile/place search, **not a general full-text post
111: search**. ReqFlow does not convert `BMW 5 Series comfort` into a guessed hashtag
112: or profile. A query-only request of that kind returns `blocked`, requiring
113: supported URLs or literal hashtags. Place search, stories, mentions, private
114: content, and login/session scraping are not implemented. The actor documents
115: limited free comments and additional paid access; approval does not prove the
116: subscription supports those features.
117: 
118: For TikTok:
119: 
120: - full `/@<handle>/video/<numeric-id>` URLs using `postURLs`;
121: - `/@<handle>` profile URLs, translated to the documented `profiles` usernames
122:   input, with `profileScrapeSections: ["videos"]` and `profileSorting: "latest"`;
123: - without URLs, documented `searchQueries` with `searchSection: "/video"` and
124:   `resultsPerPage`.
125: 
126: Short redirect links, profile follower/following scraping, related videos, paid
127: search/date filters, downloads, transcription, and AI video interpretation are
128: not enabled. The post actor receives `commentsPerPost: 0`; feedback comes from
129: the separately approved comments actor, not an automatically followed dataset
130: link or another actor.
131: 
132: Both platforms reuse **retrieved post URLs** as the comment actor input. One
133: comment run handles one retrieved post, so Instagram's documented comment rows
134: that omit a post URL can still be linked to that exact actor input. The adapter
135: retains post context even when a date filter excludes the caption, since an
136: independently dated comment on an older post can still satisfy the requested
137: range. Explicit publication dates are filtered locally; unknown dates remain
138: with a limitation when a date range was requested. Requested markets and
139: languages are not guaranteed search restrictions. No market is inferred from a
140: profile, proxy country, author name, or location of creation.
141: 
142: Replies are not requested as paid add-ons: Instagram uses
143: `includeNestedComments: false`; TikTok uses `maxRepliesPerComment: 0`. If a
144: documented Instagram nested reply is nevertheless supplied, its original text,
145: ID, date, and structural parent are retained within the result limit. TikTok
146: `repliesToId` is retained when present. Neither a mention in the text nor a reply
147: count establishes a parent ID. Complete comment/reply coverage is not promised.
148: 
149: ## Raw record mapping
150: 
151: All records validate against core `CollectedItem`. Social records use the
152: existing `sourceKind: "other_web"`; no new core category is introduced.
153: 
154: - Post `caption` (Instagram) and `text` (TikTok) are separate `passage` records.
155:   Empty captions become `metadata`. Post captions are not labeled as customer
156:   feedback and are not merged with comments.
157: - Original comment `text` is a `feedback` record. Unicode, leading/trailing
158:   whitespace, emoji, and newlines are copied verbatim, with no sentiment or
159:   inferred ownership/vehicle classification.
160: - `recordId` preserves the original post ID, Instagram comment `id`, or TikTok
161:   comment `cid`. Original numeric Instagram values also remain in metadata.
162:   Deduplication distinguishes post IDs from comment IDs.
163: - Comment `sourceId`/`threadId` identify the retrieved post; `context` retains its
164:   original ID, URL, and caption. An explicit Instagram `commentUrl` is retained
165:   as `sourceUrl`; otherwise the post URL is used. Explicit post/permalink fields
166:   are retained in metadata. A contradictory post URL is reported as malformed,
167:   rather than assigned another post's context.
168: - Instagram top-level `parentId` is the input post; supplied nested replies use
169:   the containing comment's ID. `metadata.parentUrl` preserves the known parent
170:   post/permalink URL. TikTok reply `parentId` comes only from `repliesToId`; no
171:   parent permalink is invented when the actor does not supply one.
172: - Original `timestamp`/`createTimeISO` strings are preserved. Explicit Unix
173:   `createTime` is retained and can be represented as an ISO instant when the ISO
174:   field is absent. Missing dates never use collection time as publication time.
175: - TikTok `textLanguage` is copied as reported, including its unknown-language
176:   marker. Instagram's checked post/comment outputs do not establish a language
177:   field; the adapter does not detect one.
178: - Instagram `paidPartnership`, `affiliate`, and `sponsors`, plus TikTok `isAd` and
179:   `isSponsored`, are retained when supplied. Missing flags are not converted to
180:   `false`. TikTok `locationCreated` remains raw metadata, not market attribution.
181: - Existing TikTok `videoMeta.subtitleLinks` retain language, links, source,
182:   translation attribution, and version exactly as supplied. The documented
183:   examples supply subtitle **links**, not inline timed cue text. This adapter
184:   does not fetch those files, assert they are human-authored, invent timestamps,
185:   or claim to return a video transcript. `downloadSubtitlesOptions` is
186:   `NEVER_DOWNLOAD_SUBTITLES`; machine transcription and AI summary/description
187:   options are explicitly disabled. Instagram reel transcription is not supplied
188:   by a separate, unapproved reel actor.
189: 
190: Original captions/comments are the evidence. The adapter does not infer opinions
191: from images, alt text, music, video, popularity counts, or profile information.
192: 
193: ## Run lifecycle, limits, and cost safety
194: 
195: The API was verified against the official API documentation:
196: 
197: - [Run Actor](https://docs.apify.com/api/v2/actors-runs-post)
198: - [Get run](https://docs.apify.com/api/v2/actor-run-get)
199: - [Get dataset items](https://docs.apify.com/api/v2/dataset-items-get)
200: - [Abort run](https://docs.apify.com/api/v2/actor-run-abort-post)
201: - [Authentication](https://docs.apify.com/api/v2#authentication)
202: - [Get private user data](https://docs.apify.com/api/v2/users-me-get)
203: 
204: Each actor starts asynchronously with
205: `POST /v2/actors/<owner>~<actor>/runs`, JSON input, and:
206: 
207: ```text
208: maxTotalChargeUsd = ctx.limits.maxApifyChargeUsd
209: memory = 1024 MB
210: timeout = remaining collection time in whole seconds, minimum 1 second
211: waitForFinish = 0
212: restartOnError = false
213: maxItems = bounded raw dataset item allowance
214: ```
215: 
216: Memory is fixed and bounded; a memory failure does not trigger automatic larger
217: runs. A collection deadline and `ctx.signal` bound client work. The timeout on
218: each remote run also bounds execution if the client loses connectivity. Polling
219: uses `GET /v2/actor-runs/<id>?waitForFinish=<1–5 seconds>` until `SUCCEEDED`,
220: `FAILED`, `TIMED-OUT`, or `ABORTED`. Transitional `TIMING-OUT` and `ABORTING` are
221: not treated as completion. Unknown status, changing run identity, and malformed
222: run/dataset responses are failures.
223: 
224: Completed runs, including failed/timed-out runs, can have useful partial
225: datasets. Those records are retained with a limitation. Dataset requests use
226: `GET /v2/datasets/<id>/items?format=json&clean=false&offset=<items>&limit=<items>`.
227: Pages contain at most 50 requested raw items. Offsets count **items**, not pages;
228: no `unwind`, `clean=true`, or empty/error filtering changes offset semantics.
229: Rows are validated individually, and successes survive malformed rows, later
230: page failures, and individual comment actor failures.
231: 
232: `maxResults` is a combined record limit, including captions, comments, nested
233: replies, and metadata. When comments are approved, discovery reserves up to
234: `ceil(maxResults / 2)` posts; remaining capacity is available to comments. The
235: adapter does not promise a representative or complete sample. Actor input
236: limits are per URL/query and `maxItems` is a **billing** limit, not an exact
237: output guarantee; the adapter separately bounds scanned rows and returned
238: records. Excess output is reported and not added.
239: 
240: **The Apify charge cap is per actor run, not a collection-wide dollar cap.** A
241: collection can launch post discovery plus multiple comment runs, each with the
242: specified `maxApifyChargeUsd`. Subscription charges, prior runs, reads, and other
243: account usage are not proved by this cap. A strict aggregate spending guarantee
244: requires a host-level budget policy; the current adapter contract does not
245: provide one. Immediate run costs are not reliable final accounting: the official
246: Get run documentation warns that final costs/event counts can remain preliminary
247: for roughly 10 seconds after completion. The adapter does not use preliminary
248: costs to authorize more actors or claim remaining funds.
249: 
250: Cancellation, timeout, or an interrupted known nonterminal run triggers a
251: best-effort `POST /v2/actor-runs/<id>/abort?gracefully=false`. Cleanup uses a
252: **fresh independent signal** bounded to five seconds, not the already-aborted
253: collection signal. It still uses `ctx.http`, so a denied/exhausted HTTP budget or
254: unreachable service can prevent abort. The HTTP host must honor the per-call
255: cleanup signal rather than forcibly reusing the cancelled collection signal.
256: An `ABORTING` response is not confirmation of final termination.
257: 
258: **Abort is not a refund.** Costs already incurred and work during cancellation
259: can still be billed. If abort fails or actor start succeeded but its response/run
260: ID was lost, the adapter cannot prove termination; costs may continue until the
261: remote timeout. It reports that limitation and does not silently claim cleanup.
262: The official graceful option can allow 30 more seconds, so it is not enabled.
263: Check the Apify console when termination was not confirmed.
264: 
265: Retries, timeouts, and common request budgets belong to `ctx.http`; this adapter
266: does not add retry loops. The HTTP host must not blindly replay a non-idempotent
267: actor-start POST after an ambiguous transport failure: duplicate runs may cost
268: money and no checked API contract establishes an actor-start idempotency key.
269: Ordinary adapter calls stop at the common request count; cleanup is still
270: attempted through that same service and may be rejected by its budget policy.
271: 
272: Authentication is always `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. No token is placed in
273: query parameters, actor input, metadata, logs, or returned error messages. Remote
274: error messages and run status messages are not echoed; failures name the actor
275: and safe error category instead.
276: 
277: ## Connection test and offline proof
278: 
279: `test(ctx)` calls only `GET /v2/users/me`. It validates the account response and
280: reports token authentication, never actor permissions, account spending
281: capacity, subscription features, platform access, or usage rights. This check
282: does not run an actor or change the configuration/approval/allowlist.
283: 
284: `apify.test.ts` contains deterministic synthetic fixtures using official field
285: names. It covers approval/token gates, the exact actor allowlist, async polling,
286: terminal statuses, pagination, limits, captions versus comments, Unicode and
287: newlines, IDs and explicit dates, ad flags, subtitle-link provenance, reply
288: parents, null text, search limitations, domain restrictions, partial failures,
289: cancellation/timeout cleanup, secret-free URLs/errors, and the cheap connection
290: test. The mock HTTP queue cannot perform actual network requests.
291: 
292: ```sh
293: npx vitest run packages/blocks/src/research/providers/apify.test.ts
294: npm run typecheck && npm test
295: ```
296: 
297: No live actor acceptance run has been performed. Integration wiring, settings UI,
298: shared manifests/contracts, and aggregate cost policy are outside this file-only
299: slice.
</content>

435:       return z.enum(spec.options.map((o) => o.value) as [string, ...string[]]);
436:     case "multiselect": {
437:       const values = spec.options.map((o) => o.value) as [string, ...string[]];
438:       return z
439:         .array(z.enum(values))
440:         .refine((v) => new Set(v).size === v.length, "Each option may be selected only once");
441:     }
442:     case "toggle":
443:       return z.boolean();
444:     case "list":
445:       return z
446:         .array(z.string().trim().min(1, "Entries can't be empty").max(60))
447:         .min(spec.minItems)
448:         .max(spec.maxItems);
449:     case "file":
450:       return FileRef.nullable();
451:   }
452: }

454: const paramsSchemaCache = new Map<BlockKind, z.ZodType<BlockParams>>();
455: 
456: /** Strict Zod schema for a block's params: unknown keys and wrong types are errors, not dropped. */
457: export function blockParamsSchema(kind: BlockKind): z.ZodType<BlockParams> {
458:   let schema = paramsSchemaCache.get(kind);
459:   if (!schema) {
460:     schema = isBoundaryBlockKind(kind)
461:       ? BoundaryParams
462:       : z.strictObject(
463:           Object.fromEntries(BLOCK_SPECS[kind].params.map((p) => [p.key, paramSchema(p)])),
464:         );
465:     paramsSchemaCache.set(kind, schema);
466:   }
467:   return schema;
468: }
469: 
470: export function defaultBlockParams(kind: PaletteBlockKind): BlockParams {
471:   return Object.fromEntries(
472:     BLOCK_SPECS[kind].params.map((p) => [
473:       p.key,
474:       p.type === "file" ? null : Array.isArray(p.default) ? [...p.default] : p.default,
475:     ]),
476:   );
477: }
478: 
479: /** Throws a ZodError naming the bad field. */
480: export function parseBlockParams(kind: BlockKind, params: unknown): BlockParams {
481:   return blockParamsSchema(kind).parse(params);
482: }
483: 
484: /** Whether a param field is shown, given the block's current params. */
485: export function isParamVisible(spec: ParamSpec, params: BlockParams): boolean {
486:   return !spec.visibleWhen || params[spec.visibleWhen.key] === spec.visibleWhen.equals;
487: }
488: 
489: /**
490:  * Ports of a block. Invalid params fall back to the defaults, so a broken block still renders;
491:  * `validateGraph` reports the invalid params separately.
492:  */
493: export function blockPorts(block: { kind: BlockKind; params: BlockParams }): BlockPorts {
494:   if (block.kind === "block_input") return { inputs: [], outputs: [OUT] };
495:   if (block.kind === "block_output") return { inputs: [IN], outputs: [] };
496:   const parsed = blockParamsSchema(block.kind).safeParse(block.params);
497:   const params = parsed.success ? parsed.data : defaultBlockParams(block.kind);
498:   return BLOCK_SPECS[block.kind].ports(params);
499: }

20:       }

22:         throw new Error("Advanced research scope must be a JSON object.");

24:       from.setUTCMonth(from.getUTCMonth() - Number(params.maxAgeMonths ?? 24));
25:       const document = FileRef.nullable().parse(params.document ?? null);
26:       const scope = ResearchScope.parse({

30:         markets: [params.market === "global" || !params.market ? ctx.scope.market : params.market],

34:         publishedFrom: from.toISOString().slice(0, 10),
35:         ...(document ? { documentIds: [document.fileId] } : {}),
36:         ...advanced,
37:       });
38:       const request = ResearchRequest.parse({
39:         scope: { ...scope, ...mergeResearchDomainPolicy(ctx.settings.research, scope) },
40:         agents: params.agents,
41:         limits: {
42:           maxResults: params.maxResults ?? 10,
43:           maxRequests: params.maxRequests ?? 100,
44:           maxDocumentPages: params.maxDocumentPages ?? 20,
45:           timeoutMs: params.timeoutMs ?? 120000,
46:           concurrency: params.concurrency ?? 3,
47:         },
48:       });
49:       const collectionContext = {
50:         runId: ctx.runId,
51:         signal: ctx.signal,
52:         log: ctx.log,
53:         progress: ctx.progress,
54:         planQueries: params.queryPlanning === true,
55:       };

57:       const dataset = await ctx.research.collect(request, collectionContext);

75:           out: { ...emptyPipelineData(), sources: dataset.sources, records: dataset.records },

126:   const scope = ResearchScope.parse(input);
127:   const root = searchText(

129:       scope.brand,

132:       scope.previousGeneration,

137:       scope.publishedFrom ? `publication from ${scope.publishedFrom}` : undefined,
138:       scope.publishedTo ? `publication through ${scope.publishedTo}` : undefined,
139:     ]
140:       .filter(Boolean)

148: /**

150:  * Languages, domains, URLs and dataset filters stay in scope for the source adapters to enforce.
151:  * Date/market terms are search context, not proof of a publication date or an author's location.

155:   const scope = ResearchScope.parse(input);
156:   const root = buildQueryRoot(scope);
157:   const topic = searchText(
158:     [
159:       topics[id],
160:       id === "competitor_models"
161:         ? scope.competitors
162:             .map((car) => [car.brand, car.model, car.generation].filter(Boolean).join(" "))
163:             .join(" ; ")
164:         : undefined,

166:         ? `${scope.horizonYears} year outlook`
167:         : undefined,
168:     ]
169:       .filter(Boolean)
170:       .join(" "),
171:   );
172:   const baseline = `${root} ${topic}`;
173:   if (baseline.length > 500)
174:     throw new Error("Research scope and expert context are too long for a 500-character query.");
175: 
176:   // A broad query always remains, even if the user's questions only concern complaints.
177:   const queries = [baseline];
178:   const additions = scope.keywords.length
179:     ? [scope.questions.join(" "), scope.keywords.join(" ")]
180:     : scope.questions.slice(0, 2);
181:   for (const addition of additions) {
182:     const terms = searchText(addition);
183:     if (!terms) continue;
184:     const available = 500 - baseline.length - 1;
185:     if (available < 1)
186:       throw new Error(
187:         "Research scope leaves no room for question or keyword search terms within 500 characters.",
188:       );
189:     const query = `${baseline} ${terms.slice(0, available).trim()}`;
190:     if (!queries.includes(query)) queries.push(query);
191:   }
192:   return queries;

186: const usesQueries = (provider: ResearchProviderId) =>

189:   agent: ResearchAgentId,

191:   config: ResearchProviderConfig,

199: export interface ResearchCollectorOptions {
200:   settings: Settings;
201:   credentials: Partial<Record<SecretName, string>>;
202:   /** Explicit factory-level opt-in; per-run context.planQueries takes precedence. Default: false. */
203:   queryPlanning?: boolean;
204:   documents?: ProviderContext["documents"];
205:   adapters?: Map<ResearchProviderId, ProviderAdapter>;
206:   fetchImpl?: typeof fetch;
